key_insight: LEGO proposes a lifting-free way to generate egocentric video from a single exocentric recording, avoiding explicit 3D reconstruction. Instead of deterministically projecting pixels into a point cloud, it uses a more flexible conditioning strategy that better handles missing/occluded content.
problem_solved: The paper tackles exocentric-to-egocentric video generation, where the source and target viewpoints have little overlap and large parts of the egocentric view are not directly visible in the input.
method: Removes the need for explicit depth estimation and point-cloud lifting used in prior pipelines.
Directly conditions a video diffusion model without re-rendering the scene through a reconstructed 3D representation.
Uses a lifting-free formulation to better preserve uncertainty and handle unobserved regions in the target view.
impact: This matters because it simplifies the pipeline and can improve robustness when viewpoint overlap is low. For practitioners, it offers a promising alternative to brittle reconstruction-based methods in view synthesis and video generation.

paper_title: LEGO: A Lifting-Free Approach for Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation
